conviction_note: Q3 numbers are new (no trading update, no profit warning, Peab gives no numeric guide), so I size the move at 5.5% from Peab's own report-day moves (8.2, 7.7, 7.0, 3.9, 3.1, -5.0, +4.2, -2.8 since 2024, per Finwire and Yahoo bars). The one company-level lean is that Peab's own list of orders above SEK 100m for Q3 2026 sums to SEK 1.65bn against 3.88bn in Q3 2025. Order intake decided both 2026 prints (Q1 miss -5%, Q2 beat +4.2%). That list mis-signed Q1 2026 and no Q3 consensus could be sourced, so p_up sits only slightly below 50 at 44. That gives (2*0.44-1)*5.5 = -0.66 against a finding sum of -1.1. They agree in sign, and the gap is the uncertainty in p_up.

findings.finding: Peab's own Q3 2026 list of orders above SEK 100m sums to SEK 1,649m across 9 contracts, against SEK 3,881m in Q3 2025, 2,362m in Q3 2024 and 7,712m in Q2 2026. That is the weakest Q3 on the list since at least 2023, and adding the Q3 residual of the last two years (6.3-7.8bn) implies total Q3 orders of about 8-9.5bn against 10,223m a year ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order intake decided both 2026 prints. Q1 2026: orders 15.6bn against an 18bn Bloomberg consensus, stock down more than 10% intraday and -5.0% close to close. Q2 2026: orders +39% y/y, stock +4.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side visibly does not map this list onto the reported total: Q1 2026's list was the strongest on record (7.4bn) yet consensus at 18bn still missed by 2.4bn. If the market expected a soft Q3 order print, Peab would not have run +2.7% over 5 days into the release with no disclosed short. Weakness: in Q1 2026 the list's y/y direction gave the wrong sign for the total, and the residual (own housing starts, small orders, Industry) is 60-80% of Q3 orders.
findings.independence: Partial and indirect: a company statement that own-balance-sheet housing starts now register as orders, which could fill the gap and argues the other way (Q2 report, https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/ae16177aa1abae554fa4dbaf5cd6d23f0). No independent source points the same way.

findings.finding: Peab says its shift to starting housing projects on its own balance sheet ties up more capital (Q2 cash flow before financing -663 MSEK against -560), and Q3 2025 cash flow before financing of +2,792 MSEK is a very high comparison, so Q3 cash flow is likely to print well down year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 'strong cash flow' headline print moved +0.1%. No observed Peab day where cash flow alone drove the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company said it in July. What is left is the size of the y/y fall against a record Q3 2025, which consensus may not model in full. If it were fully priced, the release-day reaction would ignore cash flow.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 release, cash flow before financing 2,792 (1,195): https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b7ad9acab2b327e0a8bdf3dc730037129&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: Swedish residential peers that reported Q3 after Peab's last release both describe better Swedish consumer demand: Bonava 'clear turnaround in the Swedish operation' with 959 (456) units sold, and JM 'försäljning till konsumenter fortsatte att utvecklas positivt i kvartalet, framför allt i den svenska verksamheten' (sales to consumers kept improving, above all in Sweden), although JM's 462 units sold missed the 517 expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peab's Housing Development is about 5% of group sales (Q2 821 MSEK of 16,778). Housing has not driven a Peab reaction in the observed prints.
findings.original_quote: JMs försäljning till konsumenter fortsatte att utvecklas positivt i kvartalet, framför allt i den svenska verksamheten. ... Antalet sålda bostäder uppgick till 462 (562), mot väntade 517.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a sector read: JM rallied from 110 to 127 after its report. Net of the rest of Peab, this touches only the small Housing Development unit.

findings.finding: Byggföretagen's October 2026 forecast (20 Oct) sees Swedish construction investment rising nearly 7% over 2026-2027, led by premises and civil engineering, which are Peab's Construction and Civil Engineering segments. Housing starts rise only from 29,500 to 31,700.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peab's qualitative market outlook has not been the stated driver of any observed reaction.
findings.original_quote: Bygginvesteringarna i bostäder, lokaler och anläggningar väntas öka med närmare sju procent under 2026 och 2027.
findings.why_not_priced: A macro forecast is broadly public, so this is mostly priced. It matters only if Peab's outlook paragraph upgrades Sweden from 'early recovery' (the July wording) and the market reads that as an outlook change.
findings.independence: Peab's own July outlook: civil engineering investment expected to rise in 2026 (https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/ae16177aa1abae554fa4dbaf5cd6d23f0)
